newsitem.title: UK: Channel Express cargo A300 gets U.S. FAA scrutiny.
newsitem.headline: Channel Express cargo A300 gets U.S. FAA scrutiny.

text.p: U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) inspectors have this week been aboard test flights of the first Channel Express A300B4, checking its airworthiness as a converted freighter, the airline said.

They want to ensure that major modifications to the airframe of the former Eastern Airlines/VIASA passenger Airbus have been satisfactorily made by British Aerospace, Channel Express's Tony Carder told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He said that a thorough inspection of conversion work on the aircraft, which is certified under the U.S. register, was required before an FAA supplemental type certificate (STC) could be issued.

"Conversion was completed by BAe Aviation Services at Filton, near Bristol, two months ago but FAA documentation checks and paperwork has taken much longer than we originally thought," said Carder, sales and marketing manager of UK airline Channel Express, a member of Dart Group Plc

He added that the current FAA inspection, which would continue until the end of the week, is mainly concentrating on the A300B4 freighter's recently-installed cargo door, the door hinges and surrounds and the strength of the aircraft's floor.

He said he felt the FAA inspection had been delayed because of the administration's recent preoccupation with an airworthiness directive it issued concerning passenger Boeing 727s converted into all-cargo configuration.
This directive is likely to affect 321 727s worldwide -- those converted from passenger aircraft by certain refurbishers other than manufacturer Boeing.
"Because of all the problems involved with the 727s, the FAA has possibly given more time to those than to the A300 conversion," Carder said.
"But we are confident that our conversion meets all the required standards. If all goes well, we are looking to a June launch into service," he said.

The 40-tonne capacity A300B4 freighter has been wet-leased (covering the hire of crew and plane) from Channel Express by British Airways World Cargo for use by the carrier on a new London Stansted-Tel Aviv service.

Carder added that once FAA certification had been acquired, the aircraft would be transferred to the UK register and he did not envisage problems in obtaining operating approval from the UK Civil Aviation Authority.
He said that Channel Express also had options with BAe for the conversion of three more A300B4 passenger planes into freighters.
